newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila health alert after office worker's suicide.
newsitem.headline: Manila health alert after office worker's suicide.

text.p: A man who committed suicide at work prompted the evacuation of hundreds of workers in a Manila office building on Friday because of fears the powdered arsenic that killed him may have entered the airconditioning system.

Romy Minase, supervisor of the 18-storey Locsin Building in the city's main business district, said arsenic powder was scattered around the 12th floor after an employee of the country's largest telephone company, Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT), committed suicide on Thursday night.
"We are recommending all offices send all of their employees home for their own safety," Minase said.
Some people who worked in the building had complained of itchiness and dizziness and there were fears this could be linked to arsenic inhalation, Minase said.
A private doctor contacted by Reuters said, however, that there was not likely to be a strong health risk from the inhalation of arsenic.
Government health experts were being asked to examine the building and its airconditioning system, Minase said.
The building also houses the British Embassy and the Manila bureau of Reuters Holdings Plc.
